incline-bench-press: an incline barbell bench press: lying on its back on a bench inclined at about 30 degrees (head end higher), feet on the floor, pressing a barbell with plates straight up above the upper chest, arms extended
decline-bench-press: a decline barbell bench press: lying on its back on a decline bench (head end lower than the hips), legs hooked under the leg pad, pressing a barbell with plates straight up above the lower chest, arms extended
db-bench-press: a dumbbell bench press: lying on its back on a flat bench, feet on the floor, pressing two dumbbells straight up above the chest, one in each hand, arms extended
incline-db-press: an incline dumbbell press: lying on its back on a bench inclined at about 30 degrees (head end higher), feet on the floor, pressing two dumbbells straight up above the upper chest, one in each hand
db-fly: a dumbbell fly, seen from a high three-quarter front angle: lying on its back on a flat bench, both arms opened wide out to the sides in a wide arc, almost level with the bench, elbows slightly bent, one dumbbell in each hand, so both outstretched arms are clearly visible
cable-fly: a standing cable fly: standing upright between two tall cable stations, one foot slightly forward, bringing the two cable handles together in front of the chest with slightly bent arms, cables running from high pulleys on each side
pec-deck: a pec deck machine fly: sitting upright on the machine seat with the back against the pad, forearms against the two padded arms, bringing the arms together in front of the chest
chest-press-machine: a seated chest press machine: sitting upright on the machine seat with the back against the pad, pushing the two handles straight forward at chest height, arms almost extended
push-up: a push-up: body in a straight plank line facing the floor, hands on the floor under the shoulders, arms extended, toes on the floor, no equipment
chest-dip: a chest dip on two parallel dip bars: holding the bars with arms bent at about 90 degrees, body lowered between the bars and leaning forward, knees bent and feet crossed behind, feet off the floor. Full-bleed image with the pure black background reaching every edge, no border or frame
pull-up: a pull-up: hanging from a horizontal pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders, pulling the body up so the chin is above the bar, legs straight down and off the floor
chin-up: a chin-up: hanging from a horizontal bar with an underhand grip (palms facing the body) at shoulder width, chin pulled above the bar, legs straight down and off the floor
lat-pulldown: a lat pulldown: sitting on the machine seat with the thighs under the knee pad, pulling a wide straight bar attached to a high cable down to the upper chest, elbows pointing down
barbell-row: a bent-over barbell row: standing with knees slightly bent and torso hinged forward almost parallel to the floor, back straight, pulling a barbell with plates up to the lower ribs
db-row: a one-arm dumbbell row, side view: one knee and the hand on the same side supported on a flat bench, the other foot planted on the floor, torso flat and parallel to the floor, the free arm rowing one dumbbell up towards the waist
seated-cable-row: a seated cable row: sitting on the floor-level bench of a low cable machine, feet on the foot plate, knees slightly bent, torso upright, pulling a close-grip handle to the stomach
t-bar-row: a T-bar row: standing over a barbell anchored to the floor at one end, knees bent, torso hinged forward, pulling the loaded free end of the bar (plates on it) up to the chest with a close handle
chest-supported-row: a chest-supported T-bar row machine, side view: the mannequin stands on the foot platform and lies face-down with its chest and stomach on an inclined padded support, both arms hanging down and pulling the two handles of the lever arm up towards the chest
straight-arm-pulldown: a straight-arm cable pulldown: standing facing a high cable pulley, hips slightly hinged, pushing a straight bar down to the thighs with straight arms
face-pull: a cable face pull: standing facing a cable pulley set at face height, pulling a rope attachment towards the face, elbows high and wide, hands beside the ears
rack-pull: a rack pull, side view: standing upright and tall in front of a power rack, both arms straight down in front of the body holding a barbell with plates against the front of the thighs, the bar clearly in front of the legs, never behind
back-extension: a back extension: on a 45-degree hyperextension bench, hips against the pad and ankles locked under the foot pads, body in a straight line, arms crossed over the chest
inverted-row: an inverted row: lying under a barbell set at waist height in a rack, holding it with straight arms, heels on the floor, body straight like a reverse plank, pulling the chest up to the bar
overhead-press: a standing barbell overhead press, front view: standing upright, feet hip-width apart, a barbell with plates pressed straight overhead with arms fully extended. Only grey and silver tones, no coloured spots
seated-db-shoulder-press: a seated dumbbell shoulder press: sitting upright on a bench with a vertical back support, pressing two dumbbells overhead, one in each hand, arms almost extended
arnold-press: an Arnold press: sitting upright on a bench with back support, dumbbells in front of the face with palms facing the body, rotating the wrists while pressing the dumbbells up
machine-shoulder-press: a seated shoulder press machine: sitting upright with the back against the pad, pressing the two machine handles straight up above the shoulders
lateral-raise: a dumbbell lateral raise: standing upright, raising two dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height with slightly bent elbows, front view so both arms are visible
cable-lateral-raise: a one-arm cable lateral raise, front view: standing upright with a low cable pulley at the side of the body, one arm raised straight out to the side (not forward) to shoulder height holding the cable handle, the other hand on the hip
front-raise: a dumbbell front raise: standing upright, raising two dumbbells straight in front of the body to shoulder height with nearly straight arms
rear-delt-fly: a bent-over rear delt fly: standing with the torso hinged forward almost parallel to the floor, raising two dumbbells out to the sides with slightly bent arms
upright-row: a barbell upright row, front three-quarter view: standing upright, the barbell with plates pulled up close to the body to chest height just under the chin, both elbows raised high above the hands and pointing out to the sides
db-shrug: a dumbbell shrug: standing upright with arms straight down holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, shoulders lifted up towards the ears
biceps-curl: a standing dumbbell biceps curl: standing upright, elbows at the sides, curling two dumbbells up towards the shoulders with palms facing up
barbell-curl: a standing barbell curl, side view at the top of the movement: elbows fixed at the sides of the torso, forearms bent upward, the barbell with plates curled up to chest height with an underhand grip. The whole body from head to feet is visible in the frame, small enough to leave margin all around
hammer-curl: a hammer curl: standing upright, elbows at the sides, curling two dumbbells up with palms facing each other (neutral grip)
incline-db-curl: an incline dumbbell curl: sitting back on a bench inclined at about 45 degrees, arms hanging down behind the torso, curling one dumbbell in each hand
preacher-curl: a preacher curl: sitting at a preacher bench with the upper arms resting on the angled pad, curling an EZ bar up towards the shoulders
cable-curl: a standing cable curl: standing upright facing a low cable pulley, elbows at the sides, curling a straight bar attachment up towards the chest
pushdown: a triceps pushdown: standing upright facing a high cable pulley, elbows tucked at the sides, pushing a short straight bar down until the arms are straight
rope-pushdown: a triceps rope pushdown: standing upright facing a high cable pulley, elbows tucked at the sides, pushing a rope attachment down and spreading its two ends apart at the bottom
skull-crusher: a skull crusher: lying on its back on a flat bench, upper arms vertical, bending the elbows to lower an EZ bar towards the forehead
overhead-triceps-extension: an overhead dumbbell triceps extension: sitting upright on a bench, holding one dumbbell with both hands behind the head, elbows pointing up
close-grip-bench-press: a close-grip bench press: lying on its back on a flat bench, feet on the floor, hands close together at shoulder width on a barbell with plates, pressing it up above the chest
bench-dip: a bench dip: hands on the edge of a flat bench behind the body, legs extended forward with heels on the floor, hips lowered below the bench, elbows bent
front-squat: a barbell front squat: standing in a deep squat with the torso upright, a barbell with plates resting on the front of the shoulders, elbows high and pointing forward
goblet-squat: a goblet squat: in a deep squat with the torso upright, holding one dumbbell vertically against the chest with both hands
hack-squat: a hack squat machine: standing on the angled foot plate with the back against the sloped back pad and the shoulders under the shoulder pads, knees bent in a squat
leg-press: a 45-degree leg press machine: sitting reclined in the seat, feet on the large angled foot plate, knees bent, pushing the sled up
romanian-deadlift: a Romanian deadlift: standing with knees slightly bent, hips pushed back, torso hinged forward with a straight back, holding a barbell with plates just below the knees with straight arms
leg-extension: a leg extension machine: sitting upright on the machine with the shins behind the ankle pad, straightening the knees to lift the pad until the legs are extended
lying-leg-curl: a lying leg curl machine: lying face down on the machine bench, the back of the ankles under the roller pad, bending the knees to curl the pad up towards the glutes
seated-leg-curl: a seated leg curl machine: sitting upright on the machine with a pad over the thighs, the back of the ankles on a roller pad, bending the knees to pull the pad down and back
walking-lunge: a walking lunge with dumbbells: one leg stepped forward with the front knee bent at 90 degrees and the back knee close to the floor, torso upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides
bulgarian-split-squat: a Bulgarian split squat: the back foot resting on a flat bench behind, the front leg bent in a deep lunge, torso upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides
standing-calf-raise: a standing calf raise machine: standing upright under the shoulder pads, the balls of the feet on the edge of the foot platform, heels raised high on the toes
seated-calf-raise: a seated calf raise machine: sitting with the knees under the padded lever, the balls of the feet on the foot platform, heels raised high
hip-thrust: a barbell hip thrust: upper back resting against the side of a flat bench, feet flat on the floor, knees bent at 90 degrees, hips lifted so the torso and thighs form a straight line, a barbell with plates across the hips
glute-bridge: a glute bridge: lying on its back on the floor, knees bent and feet flat, hips lifted so the shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line, arms on the floor at the sides, no equipment
cable-kickback: a cable glute kickback: standing facing a low cable pulley, holding the machine frame, kicking one straight leg back with the ankle strapped to the cable
plank: a forearm plank: body in a straight line facing the floor, resting on the forearms and toes, no equipment
side-plank: a side plank: lying on one side, resting on one forearm and the side of the feet, body lifted in a straight line, the free arm on the hip, front view of the body
crunch: a crunch: lying on its back on the floor, knees bent and feet flat, hands beside the head, shoulders curled up off the floor, no equipment
cable-crunch: a kneeling cable crunch: kneeling in front of a high cable pulley, holding a rope attachment beside the head, crunching the torso down towards the knees
hanging-leg-raise: a hanging leg raise: hanging from a pull-up bar with straight arms, legs raised straight in front of the body to hip height
ab-wheel-rollout: an ab wheel rollout: kneeling on the floor, holding an ab wheel with both hands, rolling it forward so the body is extended in a long straight line close to the floor
treadmill-run: running on a treadmill: mid-stride on the moving belt of a treadmill machine with handrails and a console in front, arms swinging
rowing-machine: a rowing machine (ergometer): sitting on the sliding seat, feet strapped on the foot plates, legs extended, leaning slightly back and pulling the handle to the lower ribs
stationary-bike: a stationary exercise bike: sitting on the saddle of an upright stationary bike, hands on the handlebars, pedalling
default: standing upright in a relaxed neutral stance, feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at the sides, no equipment at all, front three-quarter view; NO muscle group is highlighted: the whole body has the same even soft grey shading with only subtle uniform highlights; this is a generic picture for any exercise
